title: Lesson 24 - Teams and the Permission Model: Account Teams, Opportunity Teams, Permission Set Groups
description: Given a set of business requirements, identify the appropriate security model (sharing rules, role hierarchy, Account Teams, Opportunity Teams, permission sets, permission set groups).

questions.question: Two users share a role, but one needs two extra field permissions. What is the recommended fix?
options: Create a second profile with those field permissions
Assign a permission set that grants the extra access to the one user
Add the user to a sharing rule
questions.explanation: Permission sets are the additive, maintainable way to grant a single user extra access, while a second profile is one-per-user overhead and sharing does not control field permissions.

questions.question: You muted Read on an object in a permission set group's muting permission set. What else is muted?
options: Read and nothing else in the group
Create, Edit, Delete, View All Records, and Modify All Records
questions.explanation: Muting cascades through permission dependencies, and because Create, Edit, Delete, View All, and Modify All are unusable without read, they are muted along with it.

questions.question: A user must collaborate on one deal while the rest of the account stays hidden. What do you configure?
options: An Opportunity Team membership for that opportunity
A change to the user's role
A change to the organization-wide default
questions.explanation: An Opportunity Team grants access to that opportunity only, which fits a deal-specific need, whereas an Account Team and an OWD change would open the whole account.
